Of course. I'm ready. The mixed-content errors you're seeing are because the Unlayer editor, running on HTTPS, is trying to communicate with your local development server, which is running on HTTP.

You've already set up a reverse proxy, which is great. Now, I'll focus on configuring the backend to work with your HTTPS setup. I'll start by examining the backend server entry point to understand how it's configured.

thoughts.description: I've homed in on mixed content errors, specifically those stemming from HTTPS-served applications attempting HTTP resource loading. The error messages are stark, detailing blocked frames and cross-origin access violations. I'm now cross-referencing this with the security implications.

thoughts.subject: Pinpointing Protocol Mismatches
thoughts.description: I'm focusing on the HTTP/HTTPS protocol disparity.  The error logs precisely pinpoint the problem: a local HTTP development server attempting access from a secure HTTPS context, causing cross-origin access violations. I'm now examining the server configuration, especially the backend's `index.ts` file and the `package.json` file.  I also plan on checking `vite.config.ts` for proxy settings.

thoughts.subject: Inspecting Backend Configuration
thoughts.description: I'm now examining the backend's `index.ts` file, looking for hardcoded HTTP URLs and how the server is configured to serve content. I'll then move on to the `package.json` file to identify server dependencies. I also intend to verify that the reverse proxy is correctly configured to forward HTTPS traffic to the local backend. I will review `vite.config.ts`. The focus is ensuring the backend serves content over HTTPS to align with the editor's HTTPS context.
